# Melbourne’s leading luxury real estate agencies and prestige auctioneers

For prestige residential property in Melbourne, I would start with **Kay & Burton, Marshall White, RT Edgar, Melbourne Sotheby’s International Realty and Christie’s International Real Estate**\. For auctioneering, I would shortlist experienced prestige agents with strong auction records, alongside independent specialists who can be engaged to call an auction.

The key distinction is that the best-known luxury brand is not automatically the best performer for every property. The right choice depends on the suburb, price bracket, buyer profile, and the individual agent’s recent results.

## 1\. Leading prestige real estate agencies

Shortlist based on prestige-market positioning, reported high-value transactions, specialist coverage and recent industry recognition — not a definitive audited ranking.

Website: [theauctioneer.com.au](https://theauctioneer.com.au/)

## 3\. Where the strongest prestige sales activity is concentrated

Melbourne’s established blue-chip suburbs remain the logical starting point for finding agents with relevant high-value transaction experience.



- **Toorak and Armadale\:** Trophy homes, significant landholdings and high-end architectural residences.
- **Brighton and Bayside\:** Luxury family homes, waterfront properties and large renovated residences.
- **Hawthorn, Kew and Canterbury\:** Premium family homes, heritage properties and substantial established residences.
- **South Yarra and the CBD fringe\:** Prestige apartments, penthouses and architect-designed residences.

Toorak led Victoria for \$5 million-plus home sales in 2025, with Brighton and Kew also recording substantial activity. [estateguide.online](https://estateguide.online/news/victoria-prestige-property-market-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. How to identify the actual top performers

If you are appointing an agent to sell a prestige property, I would rank candidates using these measures rather than brand reputation alone.

| Measure | What to ask for |
|--------|--------|
| Recent comparable sales | Three to five sales in the same suburb and similar price bracket within the past 12 months |
| Auction performance | Auctions conducted, sold under the hammer, passed in and sold afterward |
| Price achieved | Final sale price compared with the original appraisal and the reserve |
| Buyer competition | Number of qualified bidders and genuine active bidders |
| Campaign execution | Marketing strategy, database reach, private inspections and buyer follow-up |
| Fee structure | Commission, marketing costs and any separate auctioneer fee |


One important current consideration: Victoria introduced auction-law changes effective 1 October 2026, including a requirement for sellers to disclose their reserve price seven days before auction. Confirm the applicable requirements and how your agent will manage compliance before signing an authority. [www.heraldsun.com.au](https://www.heraldsun.com.au/real-estate/victoria/melbourne/victorias-new-auction-laws-spark-chaos-and-confusion/news-story/e29d2e8ffaabc2051be676fc7a5375ac?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.heraldsun.com.au](https://www.heraldsun.com.au/real-estate/victoria/melbourne/melbourne-auction-market-worst-in-years-as-new-laws-hit/news-story/8080c2e95ca1d98c0f5208604dba8d71?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

- **For a trophy home in Toorak\:** Interview Kay & Burton, Marshall White and RT Edgar.
- **For an auction-driven prestige campaign\:** Compare Marshall White with a leading local agent from Kay & Burton, then assess the named auctioneer who will actually call the auction.
- **For an internationally marketable luxury property\:** Add Melbourne Sotheby’s International Realty and Christie’s International Real Estate to the shortlist.
- **For independent auctioneering\:** Interview The Auction Company and The Auctioneer, requesting comparable prestige auction results.

The final choice should be based on the individual agent’s track record in your exact suburb and price range, not just the agency’s overall reputation.

**What suburb and approximate property value are you interested in?** For example, Toorak at \$5–10 million versus Brighton at \$3–5 million could lead to quite different agent and auctioneer shortlists.

search_results.title: Victoria's new auction laws spark 'chaos' and confusion
search_results.description: Victoria's recent auction law changes, which require sellers to disclose their reserve price seven days before an auction, have triggered widespread confusion and criticism. The legislation, effective from October 1 after a grace period, was intended to enhance transparency and curb underquoting. However, critics like auctioneer Andy Reid and agents such as Daniel D'Assisi argue the changes were rushed and are generating chaos. They highlight loopholes, including the ability of sellers to alter reserve prices last-minute and buyer misperceptions about pricing flexibility. The Real Estate Institute of Victoria reported a preliminary clearance rate of 55.5% from 371 early results, with a significant drop in auction volumes—down 53% compared to the previous year. Experts predict a shift toward private sales due to declining confidence in the auction process. Despite the challenges, some realtors believe the market will stabilize as stakeholders adjust to the new system. Government representatives, including Consumer Affairs Minister Tim Richardson, defend the reforms as a step towards stopping deceptive sales tactics. The coming weeks are expected to determine the true impact of the legislation on Melbourne’s real estate landscape.

search_results.title: Melbourne auction market worst in years as new laws hit
search_results.description: Melbourne’s auction market has hit a three-year low this October, with only 452 homes scheduled for auction, compared to 236 in the same period in 2023. The clearance rate has dropped to 49.3%, indicating a struggling real estate sector. New laws requiring homeowners to disclose reserve prices seven days before auctions have added to the confusion, according to industry experts. Barry Plant’s chief auctioneer, James Hatzimoisis, and REIV CEO Toby Balazs criticized the legislation as unclear and poorly timed, noting that buyer uncertainty and market complexity are compounded by the new rules. Realestate.com.au data reveals a 14% drop in new listings amid rising property sales times and falling home prices. The median home price has decreased to $819,000—a 5.2% drop from the previous year. Economist Angus Moore links these challenges to recent interest rate hikes and changes in federal property tax policy, which have reduced buyer demand and borrowing capacity. The REIV is working with Consumer Affairs Victoria to educate agents on navigating the new legislative requirements, though the market remains unsettled.

search_results.title: Christian Brothers' Parkville estate hits market for $25m
search_results.description: The Christian Brothers have listed their 7119 square meter Parkville estate for $25 million. Located on The Avenue, the property includes a circa-1870s mansion and the Mt Sion building, formerly used as an aged care facility for retired brothers. Marketed by Colliers agents on behalf of the Christian Brothers Oceania Province, it is described as the largest residential landholding in Parkville available for private acquisition and is offered with vacant possession. The Christian Brothers, who arrived in Melbourne in 1868, are selling the estate as part of a broader effort to address $774 million in claims from historic sexual abuse survivors tied to their past institutions. The site has attracted interest from aged care operators, developers, and high-net-worth individuals. It offers potential for adaptive uses such as education, healthcare, or residential development, though any redevelopment must consider its heritage significance. Expressions of interest close on November 19.

search_results.title: Stockland estate sales slow down amid housing woes
search_results.description: Stockland, a major Australian property developer, reported a 71% year-on-year drop in housing estate inquiries during the September 2026 quarter, falling to 10,452, a level lower than during the 2022/23 rate hike trough. Net sales are 35% below their December 2025 peak, which was boosted by the federal government's 5% deposit scheme. The slowdown is attributed to rising interest rates, federal tax changes, cost-of-living pressures, and housing affordability issues. Despite these conditions, Stockland is maintaining its full-year housing settlement targets of 7,300-8,300 lots and expects development margins of around 20%. The firm recorded 1,506 net sales and 828 settlements in the September quarter, with conversion rates improving despite lower inquiries. It is also expanding into higher-density developments and pursuing data centre deals. Nationally, new home sales dropped 17.5% in the quarter, and the industry’s cancellation rate rose to 13.6% in September. Analysts and executives highlighted that the sector's challenges reflect broader economic conditions, which continue to pressure buyers and developers alike. Stockland projects stable earnings for fiscal 2027, with funds from operations per security guidance at 38-39 cents and distributions at 25.2 cents.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: Unsold super-luxury homes pile up as supply outpaces demand
search_results.description:
The Indian super-luxury housing market is experiencing a significant surge in unsold inventory, particularly in metropolitan areas like Mumbai, Bengaluru, and the National Capital Region (NCR). Properties priced between Rs 20 crore and Rs 50 crore are piling up due to aggressive project launches and waning demand. As per Knight Frank, Mumbai witnessed a 70% increase in unsold inventory from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026, with NCR seeing a 16-fold spike. Across the top eight cities, stock rose 86% over two years, with current inventory overhang at 14 quarters, up from eight quarters two to three years ago.

Experts attribute this trend to high land acquisition costs leading developers to launch luxury projects in order to protect margins. Although launch volumes in 2026 increased nearly 200% year-on-year, analysts caution that continued rapid development could result in future oversupply. Changing investment preferences among high-net-worth individuals and economic factors like weaker equity markets are also slowing purchase decisions. While some developers argue the oversupply is limited to specific micro-markets, escalating property and land prices and increased competition are narrowing the buyer base. Going forward, success in this segment will rely heavily on strategic pricing, location, and project differentiation.

Melbourne’s established blue-chip suburbs remain the logical starting point for finding agents with relevant high-value transaction experience.

items.markdown:
- **Toorak and Armadale\:** Trophy homes, significant landholdings and high-end architectural residences.
- **Brighton and Bayside\:** Luxury family homes, waterfront properties and large renovated residences.
- **Hawthorn, Kew and Canterbury\:** Premium family homes, heritage properties and substantial established residences.
- **South Yarra and the CBD fringe\:** Prestige apartments, penthouses and architect-designed residences.

Toorak led Victoria for \$5 million-plus home sales in 2025, with Brighton and Kew also recording substantial activity. [estateguide.online](https://estateguide.online/news/victoria-prestige-property-market-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. How to identify the actual top performers

If you are appointing an agent to sell a prestige property, I would rank candidates using these measures rather than brand reputation alone.

sources.title: Victoria’s Prestige Property Market in 2026: Toorak’s Long Game

items.markdown:
| Measure | What to ask for |
|--------|--------|
| Recent comparable sales | Three to five sales in the same suburb and similar price bracket within the past 12 months |
| Auction performance | Auctions conducted, sold under the hammer, passed in and sold afterward |
| Price achieved | Final sale price compared with the original appraisal and the reserve |
| Buyer competition | Number of qualified bidders and genuine active bidders |
| Campaign execution | Marketing strategy, database reach, private inspections and buyer follow-up |
| Fee structure | Commission, marketing costs and any separate auctioneer fee |

items.markdown:
One important current consideration: Victoria introduced auction-law changes effective 1 October 2026, including a requirement for sellers to disclose their reserve price seven days before auction. Confirm the applicable requirements and how your agent will manage compliance before signing an authority. [www.heraldsun.com.au](https://www.heraldsun.com.au/real-estate/victoria/melbourne/victorias-new-auction-laws-spark-chaos-and-confusion/news-story/e29d2e8ffaabc2051be676fc7a5375ac?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.heraldsun.com.au](https://www.heraldsun.com.au/real-estate/victoria/melbourne/melbourne-auction-market-worst-in-years-as-new-laws-hit/news-story/8080c2e95ca1d98c0f5208604dba8d71?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

- **For a trophy home in Toorak\:** Interview Kay & Burton, Marshall White and RT Edgar.
- **For an auction-driven prestige campaign\:** Compare Marshall White with a leading local agent from Kay & Burton, then assess the named auctioneer who will actually call the auction.
- **For an internationally marketable luxury property\:** Add Melbourne Sotheby’s International Realty and Christie’s International Real Estate to the shortlist.
- **For independent auctioneering\:** Interview The Auction Company and The Auctioneer, requesting comparable prestige auction results.

The final choice should be based on the individual agent’s track record in your exact suburb and price range, not just the agency’s overall reputation.

**What suburb and approximate property value are you interested in?** For example, Toorak at \$5–10 million versus Brighton at \$3–5 million could lead to quite different agent and auctioneer shortlists.
